steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Last night wasn't the first time Michael's come looking for you, was it?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: You haven't been in Wrankwood for long, and you're certainly not the type who would have meddled with something so far outside the scope your duties, if he hadn't been pestering you.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: He came to me the day after Dalton died and I took over the prop team.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: He wanted to leave without going through the normal process, and without anyone noticing.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Without, like, telling Miss Stone or going through the contract cancellation and exit procedures?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: But he's the lead actor. Someone was bound to find out, and he'd have to pay the contract penalty anyway.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Unless... something here scared him more than paying the penalty.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: He said since the prop team had access to all the tools and was familiar with the structure of the plate, he wondered if I could...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: If you could think of a way.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I mean, I'm sure you could, but Michael's not done with his scenes yet. If he really got away and Miss Stone found out you helped him... she wouldn't let you off the hook easy.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: She could even end your career in Wrankwood!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: What would your sister think?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: My sister...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Didn't you say the rest of your family was against you coming to Wrankwood, and she's the only one who cheered you on?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: You have to make it, and not just to prove your family wrong.

spans.text: to make it, and not just to prove your family wrong.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I just don't want to disappoint my sister. I want her to be happy for me.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: S-So don't be mad, Tippi...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Please?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I'm just mad that you were hiding stuff from me.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I know you'd never agree to Michael's demands. You just didn't know how to refuse him... I can help with that.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Alright, Tippi. I've never seen you so angry...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Sh-Should we watch a movie together?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: ...You want to sneak off the plate with me?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Yeah, babe. After we spend some quality time here, we can go and pack up right away.

spans.text: Yeah, babe. After we spend some
here, we can go and pack up right away.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Even if that prop girl really does find a way for you to circumvent the exit procedures... how do you expect to avoid the penalty for breaching your contract?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Shooting isn't over yet, and you know Greta. She'll make you pay an arm and a leg!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Who cares about some stupid contract when there's a killer on the loose?!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Dalton's dead, Shelly's dead... how long do you think it'll be before you and I are next?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: We both watched and did nothing when Laura died five years ago.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Whether the killer is her lover, her dad, or some self-righteous vigilante, he's clearly after everyone who was involved!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: He wants us to repent and pay for what we did!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: I can take you away from this awful place, babe. We have our whole future ahead of us.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Ha, how romantic of you.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: But since when has your love been so deep?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: So even when you were winking at Melanie, and flirting with Anna from stage design and Mila from logistics...

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: You're telling me you were seriously thinking about spending the rest of your life with me?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: D-Does that matter right now?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Of course it does—I'm not going, Michael.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: And neither are you.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: You know how hard it was to get you a lead role in one of Greta's films? And not just one, but three at once!

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Play this right, and you'll be a bona fide Wrankwood movie star!

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: There'll be another chance...

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Look at me, Michael.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Your costume in The Death of Lady Dupont is even more exquisite and eye-catching than Melanie's, the title character.

spans.text: is even more exquisite and eye-catching than Melanie's, the title character.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Your perfume, what you wore to fashion week—I bought all of that with my own money. Even those fake ears and tail that let you pass as a Vulpo came from me...

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Without me, the public will find out that this 'Michael' product suddenly doesn't seem so shiny anymore.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: We've been together for five years. I gave up everything for you. I've spent so much of my savings, and I'm not getting any younger... I can't afford to wait for 'another chance'.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: I love you, Michael. So don't let me down.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You... love me?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You were glad when Melanie publicly revealed our relationship the day Dalton died, weren't you?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: To everyone else, I'm the troublemaking playboy, while you're the poor, suffering girlfriend who gave everything only to get nothing in return but mockery.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: How very sympathetic, huh?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: And what part of that is a lie?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You said it yourself: you're just investing in a product. Investment costs money.

spans.text: You said it yourself: you're just investing in a product.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You'd have invested in Dalton instead, wouldn't you, if he hadn't become a hopeless drunk?

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You're just a parasite looking for a host, Marion.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: This is stupid... And I'm stupid too.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Well, I guess that's it for us. You can stay if you want—I'm outta here.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Oh, and here's a tip: if you're looking for your next investment, try that pretty boy Lucian. He caught the entire crew's attention his first time in front of a camera. He's the real deal.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: The moment you walk out of here, I'm reporting you to Greta.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You cold-hearted lunatic. Are you not afraid of the killer?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: And why should I be?

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: Five years ago, I didn't even know why Laura fell to her death until later.

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: You're the one who watched and did nothing, not me.

spans.text: the one who watched and did nothing, not me.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Marion
steps.text: What are you looking at, Michael?
Rage overcomes the 'Vulpo' like a tidal wave. He sees a fire axe in a corner of the makeup room and clenches his fists.

steps.name: Tippi & Moira
steps.text: Ah—

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Why would they go down into the power deck?! Sure, there were mannequins all over the surface, but there had to have been a better plan, right Molly?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I agree.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: There's nowhere to run from the Wraith in the tight spaces of a nomadic city's underground structure.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: In the end, it found them one by one and hung them from the ducts to await a slow death in the endless darkness...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I went to one of the cast's interviews, and they said it was inspired by the rituals of certain Columbian wasteland tribes. Something about atonement and judgment...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Well, how they got there was kinda dumb, but I did like the segment in the power deck.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Because it was all shot on location!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Rumor has it that they ran out of cash, so they snuck into another film's studio plate and finished the shooting there... Exciting, right?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Wait... but I've seen this movie in theaters. Why don't I remember any of these scenes?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Because we're watching a copy of the original reel that was sent to the ratings agencies!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: How did you even get your hands on something like that?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: It's, like, a basic skill for a true horror fan!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: You're hiding something, Tippi...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: You know so much about the industry and all the ins-and-outs of Wrankwood. How does a background painter get so much insider knowledge?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: How can you do this to me, Molly?!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I share my super-secret treasure with you, hoping to make you happy, and all I get is an interrogation? *Sob*...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Aw, don't cry, I won't ask anymore, alright?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Let's just focus on the movie... so stop looking away from the screen!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Heh, you noticed.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Sorry, there's just been so much going on with the film crew lately, I'm... I'm a little nervous...

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm here for you, girl!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: You sure are!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Feeling better now?

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Okay, listen up, Molly.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: No matter who I am, one thing's for sure: I'm your best friend on this crew.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: So if there's a killer on the loose, I'll protect you!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And if work's not going well, we can do it together. We'll make our names as Wrankwood's golden horror duo, Tippi the spray-painter and Moira the prop-maker!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: And when we're really close, I'll take you to meet my family... Although I don't know if you'll be scared or surprised!

spans.text: close, I'll take you to meet my family... Although I don't know if you'll be scared or surprised!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Then I'll introduce you to my sister too!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: We'll share stories of Wrankwood while she peels us apples. She can peel one without breaking the skin in under half a minute! I know you'll love her!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Now there's an offer I can't refuse!
The old TV lights up both the darkened room and their faces. Terrifying sounds echo throughout, but take nothing away from their smiles.
They cuddle up against one another, fighting their fear with a much more familiar 'fear', and dreaming of the future of their budding friendship.
It is a rare, quiet evening.

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: Why is the set so dark?

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: *Sigh* I should've asked Moira. She's always here early, and she knows where all the switches are.

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: The prop room isn't that far, is it? Have I been going around in circles? ...Something doesn't seem right.

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: Huh? Am I hearing things?
The sound of water dripping echoes through the empty set as though answering Hautin's question, but such 'response' serves only to increase her confusion and fear.
She knows there are no water pipes above her, but the sound she is hearing is definitely coming from nearby.

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: Wh-Who's there?!

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: Is this another one of those stupid pranks you'll laugh at me over drinks after work for?

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: C-Come out now and I won't hold it against you! Or don't tell me Moira's in on it too? She's just a kid, how could you make her—

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: Ouch—

Hautin falls backwards to the ground. Only then does she realize that she is wearing a flashlight on her belt. But she barely has time to laugh at herself before she smells a strong, sweet scent accompanied by a tang of iron.
Frightened, she stands up and turns on her flashlight—
A breeze sways the ropes. Hanging down from them are two familiar and strangely quiet figures.
The two lovers, Michael and Marion, subject of much of the crew's gossip, have met their deaths with their backs against each other.
Through the faint light, Hautin sees their faces, their expressions, the way they sway through the air, and the dancing specks of dust...
It is indescribably eerie, and somehow... sacred.
She remembers what Tippi said when she joined one of her movie sessions...
In the rituals of certain Columbian wasteland tribes, hanging represents both judgment of the dead, and a warning for the living.
Until the scorching sun cracks their corpses open, until all believe they deserved their punishment, until the ropes can no longer bear the weight of their sin—
Thump.

steps.name: Unlucky Stagehand
steps.text: H-Help! Somebody! Anybody!
The unlucky stagehand runs outside. As she does, a thought flashes through her mind—
What an absurd morning.
